### The first record proves the domain is yours

Anyone can point a domain's MX at us; only its owner can publish the token we give you. Nothing is checked, and no mail is accepted, until it appears. The MX record then routes your mail, and SPF lets receivers trust what you send.

### Sending adds its own records

When you enable sending, the domain page issues three DKIM CNAME records and a bounce subdomain, unique to your domain. Copy them from the page, or let the Cloudflare one-click setup publish everything for you.

### We check them for you [...] AI companion. Experimental. The reply companion is switched on per account by an owner or admin. Drafts and rewrites draw on one monthly amount of AI, shown as a percentage used; how much each plan includes, and how it is measured, may change while it settles. On Free it starts once the account has sent or received 20 messages.

More than 50 people? Get in touch.

Setup

## Three records. Then it's yours.

Typical propagation 5–30 min · checked every ten seconds

| Type | Name | Value | Prio |
 ---  --- |
| TXT | \_foundermail |  | — |
| MX | @ | smtp.foundermail.mx | 10 |
| TXT | @ | v=spf1 include:foundermail.mx ~all | — |
| TXT | \_dmarc | v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com | — | [...] ### Can your API send email?

Yes. The REST API and the MCP server can send from your mailboxes, and they can also just write a draft for a person to send — a key scoped to drafting alone cannot send at all. Sending goes through the same rules as the dashboard: most domains may only reply to people who have written in, and every message counts against your plan's allowance. It is not a transactional or bulk sender; use a service built for that.

### Who is behind this?

Webco S.r.l.s., a one-founder company in Italy. FounderMail's mail servers are the same code that runs DevInbox, our other product; the dashboard on top is new.

## Point your MX at us and see.

Free plan, no card, unlimited mailboxes. If it isn't better than what you have, the records take two minutes to undo.

results.title: Getting started · FounderMail docs
results.content:
## 2. Add your domain

On first sign-in the wizard asks for the domain you want mail on: `yourdomain.com`, not `mail.yourdomain.com`. Later, domains are added from Domains → Add domain.

Adding a domain creates a claim. Nothing is verified, and no mail is accepted, until you prove you hold the domain by publishing the ownership record below.

## 3. Publish the DNS records

The wizard shows the records with the exact values to copy, written the way your DNS provider's form expects them (it detects Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap, Amazon Route 53 and Google Cloud DNS from your name servers). Add them at whoever hosts your DNS. [...] If your DNS is on Cloudflare, the domain page can add every record for you with an API token scoped to that zone. It shows what it will add and remove before it touches anything. See Domains and DNS.

Replace any existing MX records rather than adding ours beside them: mail goes to whichever host the sending server picks, and two hosts means some of your mail lands at the old one.

## 4. Verify

The wizard checks for the records every ten seconds and shows each one turning green as it lands. You do not have to stay on the page; the domain page has a Verify domain button for later. Verification happens in two parts: [...] | Type | Name | Value | Priority | Purpose |
 ---  --- 
| TXT | `_foundermail` | the token shown on your domain page | — | Proves you own the domain. Required. |
| MX | `@` | `smtp.foundermail.mx` | 10 | Routes your mail to FounderMail. Required. |
| TXT | `@` | `v=spf1 include:foundermail.mx ~all` | — | Authorises FounderMail to send for your domain. Required for sending. |
| TXT | `_dmarc` | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com` | — | Tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail. Recommended. |

Underscore names. Some DNS panels refuse a record name that starts with an underscore. If yours does, put the same ownership value in a TXT record on the domain itself (`@`); the verifier checks both places.

results.title: Privacy Policy · FounderMail
results.content:
## 4. The mail we host for you

FounderMail's purpose is to receive, store, present and send email for your domains. In doing so we necessarily store the content of every message: headers, bodies, attachments, drafts, and the original bytes as they arrived. We also derive data from it: a text preview, a search index, and the contact and organisation records that group mail by sender.

Automated processing of mail content is limited to what the service needs: [...] | Cloudflare | DNS for our own domains; bot protection (Turnstile) on sign-up and on the website forms you embed; cookieless analytics on the marketing site | The IP address and browser signals of whoever completes a Turnstile challenge, and anonymous page-view counts on foundermail.io. If you use the Cloudflare one-click DNS setup, the API token you paste is used for that request and not stored. |
| Sentry | Error tracking | Error reports as described in section 3, in the EU (Germany) |
| Anthropic, PBC | The optional AI assistant, for accounts that turn it on | The conversation being replied to, the contact's details and the notes given to the assistant, sent when a draft is asked for; processed in the United States and not used to train models | [...] | Provider | Role | What they process |
 --- 
| Microsoft Azure | Hosting: application servers, database, blob storage | Everything the service stores, including mail content, in the United States (West US 2 region) |
| Amazon Web Services (Simple Email Service) | Delivery of mail you send | The outgoing message and its recipients, and your domain's DKIM signing keys, in the EU (Ireland) region |
| Stripe | Payments | Your name, email, card details (entered on Stripe's pages) and invoices |
| Resend | Sending account emails | Your address and the account email's content |
